title: The efficacy of telemedicine in outpatient care for cancer patients
author: Yasuaki Uemoto
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b38qqrvw

steps.title: Define Study Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Establish the parameters for selecting articles for the systematic review.

substeps.instruction: Include only randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing telemedicine via videoconferencing for cancer patients in outpatient care provided by medical professionals.
Include all languages, countries, and publication types (published, unpublished, conference abstracts, letters).
Exclude quasi-randomization, observational studies, and case series.
Include cancer patients in any outpatient setting (perioperative, postoperative, metastatic) regardless of age, sex, or race.
Exclude patients receiving telemedicine for non-cancer conditions.
Define intervention as videoconferencing replacing all or part of usual care, conducted by doctors, nurses, or psychotherapists.
Define control as face-to-face care in an outpatient clinic.

steps.title: Identify Primary and Secondary Outcomes
steps.instruction: Define the specific metrics to be extracted from the included studies.

substeps.instruction: Primary Outcomes: Patient satisfaction (NRS-based questionnaire), Cost in money (average travel spend in $), and Outpatient attendance proportion.

Secondary Outcomes: Medical professional satisfaction (NRS-based), Cost in time (average travel time in minutes), Time devoted to outpatient care (minutes), Patient wait time (minutes), Depression score (validated questionnaires like HAM-D and IDS-C), Intensity of cancer pain (Brief Pain Inventory), and All adverse events (as defined by original authors or unexpected hospitalization proportion).

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Execute a comprehensive search for relevant studies across electronic databases and other resources.

substeps.instruction: Search electronic databases: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via PubMed, EMBASE via Dialog, and CINAHL using the strategies detailed in Appendices 1, 2, and 3.
Search for ongoing or unpublished trials via WHO International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) and ClinicalTrials.gov using strategies in Appendices 4 and 5.
Review reference lists of eligible studies, international guidelines, and articles citing eligible studies.
Contact original authors for unpublished or additional data.

steps.title: Screen Studies and Extract Data
steps.instruction: Systematically select eligible studies and extract technical data using a standardized process.

substeps.instruction: Screen titles and abstracts independently (two reviewers: Uemoto Y, Yamanaka T), followed by full-text assessment.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or a third arbiter (Kikawa Y, Kataoka Y, or Wada Y).
Perform independent data extraction using a standardized form pre-checked with 10 randomly selected studies.
Extract information on study design, population, interventions, and outcomes.
Resolve extraction disagreements via discussion or a third arbiter.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of the included studies.

substeps.instruction: Two reviewers (Uemoto Y, Yamanaka T) independently evaluate risk of bias using the Risk of Bias 2 tool.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or a third arbiter (Kikawa Y, Kataoka Y, or Wada Y).

steps.title: Analyze Data and Measure Treatment Effects
steps.instruction: Synthesize the data using statistical methods to determine efficacy.

substeps.instruction: Pool mean differences and 95% CIs for continuous variables (satisfaction, cost, attendance, time, depression, and pain).
Use standard mean differences (SMDs) if different scales were used across studies.
Summarize adverse events based on original article definitions without performing meta-analysis.
For cluster-RCTs, reduce sample size for continuous data while keeping means and standard deviations unchanged.
For randomized cross-over studies, use data from the first period only.

steps.title: Handle Missing Data and Statistics
steps.instruction: Address gaps in reported data to ensure analysis robustness.

substeps.instruction: Request missing data from original authors.
Do not impute missing continuous outcome data per Cochrane handbook recommendations; analyze available data.
Calculate standard deviation from standard error or p-values using the Altman method.
If unavailable, calculate standard deviation using confidence intervals and t-values per Cochrane handbook or validated methods.
Verify validity of these calculations via sensitivity analysis.

steps.title: Evaluate Heterogeneity and Reporting Bias
steps.instruction: Assess the consistency of results and the potential for publication bias.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate statistical heterogeneity via forest plot visual inspection and the I2 statistic (0-40%: low; 30-60%: moderate; 50-90%: substantial; 75-100%: considerable).
Perform Cochrane Chi2 test (Q-test) for I2; P < 0.10 is statistically significant.
Compare outcomes defined in trial protocols with reported outcomes to assess reporting bias.
Assess publication bias via funnel plot visual inspection and Egger test (only if ≥10 trials or varying sample sizes are present).

steps.title: Perform Meta-Analysis and Subgroup Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct the final statistical synthesis and explore modifiers.

substeps.instruction: Perform meta-analysis using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4.1) with a random-effects model.
Conduct subgroup analysis for primary outcomes based on cancer type, rural vs. urban residence, and use of specific applications with the videoconferencing system.

steps.title: Conduct Sensitivity Analysis
steps.instruction: Test the robustness of the primary outcome results.

substeps.instruction: Exclude studies using imputed statistics.
Verify robustness regarding missing participants using informative missingness odds ratios.
Analyze only participants who completed the study with complete data.

steps.title: Generate Summary of Findings
steps.instruction: Finalize the evidence certainty and create a summary table.

substeps.instruction: Two reviewers (Uemoto Y, Wada Y) evaluate certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach, with a third arbiter (Kikawa Y or Kataoka Y) if needed.
Create a Summary of Findings table for patient satisfaction, cost of money, attendance rate, medical professional satisfaction, time devoted to care, wait time, and pain intensity.
